title: Psalms Chapter 86 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 86 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 86 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 86.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 86 as stated in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:1 identifies the prayer as 'A Prayer of David,' indicating David as the author.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:1, how does David describe himself when asking the LORD to hear him?
questions.correctAnswer: Poor and needy
questions.explanation: David says, 'for I am poor and needy,' showing his humility and dependence on God.

questions.question: What does David ask God to preserve in Psalms 86:2?
questions.correctAnswer: His soul
questions.explanation: David prays, 'Preserve my soul; for I am holy,' asking God to protect his inner being.

questions.question: In Psalms 86:2, David refers to himself as what in relation to God?
questions.correctAnswer: A servant
questions.explanation: David calls himself 'thy servant that trusteth in thee,' emphasizing his reliance on God.

questions.question: How often does David say he cries unto the LORD according to Psalms 86:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Daily
questions.explanation: David says, 'for I cry unto thee daily,' showing his continual prayer life.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to do to his soul in Psalms 86:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice
questions.explanation: David prays, 'Rejoice the soul of thy servant,' asking God to bring joy.

questions.question: What action does David take towards the LORD in Psalms 86:4?
questions.correctAnswer: He lifts up his soul
questions.explanation: David says, 'for unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul,' expressing trust and devotion.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:5, what two qualities does the LORD have towards those who call upon Him?
questions.correctAnswer: Good and ready to forgive
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive,' highlighting God's mercy.

questions.question: Who does the LORD show mercy to according to Psalms 86:5?
options: All them that call upon Him
questions.correctAnswer: All them that call upon Him
questions.explanation: The verse says God is 'plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee,' indicating inclusivity.

questions.question: In Psalms 86:6, what does David ask the LORD to do with his prayer?
options: Give ear and attend to it
questions.correctAnswer: Give ear and attend to it
questions.explanation: David says, 'Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications,' requesting God's attentive listening.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 86:1, David describes himself as wealthy and strong.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David describes himself as 'poor and needy,' not wealthy or strong.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 86:3 says David cries unto the LORD daily.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'for I cry unto thee daily,' confirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 86:6 asks the LORD to ignore the supplications of David.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David requests that God 'Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications,' not to ignore them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 86:2 refers to David as a servant who trusts in God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David calls himself 'thy servant that trusteth in thee,' showing his trust in God.

questions.question: In Psalms 86, which request does David make first?
options: Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me
Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me
questions.explanation: The first request David makes is in verse 1: 'Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 86 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 86 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:7, what will the psalmist do in the day of trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: Call upon the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:7 states that in the day of trouble, the psalmist will call upon the Lord, trusting that God will answer him. This shows reliance on God in difficult times, consistent with the themes of trust and prayer throughout Psalms 86:1-7.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:8 describe the Lord in comparison to other gods?
options: There is none like Him and no works like His
He is one among many gods
He is less powerful than other gods
He is a god of wrath only
questions.correctAnswer: There is none like Him and no works like His
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:8 declares that among the gods there is none like the Lord and no works like His, emphasizing God's uniqueness and incomparable power, in line with the psalmist's praise of God's greatness in verses 9 and 10.

questions.question: What is promised in Psalms 86:9 about all nations made by God?
options: They shall come and worship before the Lord
They shall fight against each other
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come and worship before the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:9 states that all nations made by God shall come and worship before Him and glorify His name, highlighting the universal recognition of God's sovereignty as also celebrated in verses 8 and 10.

questions.question: What reason does Psalms 86:10 give for praising God’s greatness?
options: Because He does wondrous things and is God alone
Because He changes His mind often
questions.correctAnswer: Because He does wondrous things and is God alone
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:10 explains God’s greatness by His wondrous deeds and His uniqueness as God alone, reinforcing the psalmist’s call to worship seen in verses 8 and 9.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:11, what does the psalmist ask God to teach him?
options: God’s way, so he may walk in His truth
questions.correctAnswer: God’s way, so he may walk in His truth
questions.explanation: In Psalms 86:11, the psalmist requests God to teach him His way so he can walk in truth and have a heart united in fearing God’s name, reflecting humility and obedience as key virtues.

questions.question: What does Psalms 86:12 say the psalmist will do with all his heart?
options: Praise the Lord and glorify His name forevermore
questions.correctAnswer: Praise the Lord and glorify His name forevermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:12 expresses the psalmist’s commitment to praise God with all his heart and glorify His name forevermore, showing wholehearted worship and devotion as also encouraged by God’s mercy in earlier verses.

questions.question: What connection can be made between Psalms 86:11 and Psalms 86:12 regarding the psalmist’s spiritual walk?
options: Learning God's way leads to wholehearted praise and glorification
questions.correctAnswer: Learning God's way leads to wholehearted praise and glorification
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:11 asks for instruction in God’s way to walk in truth and have a heart united in fear of God’s name, which naturally results in the wholehearted praise and glorification described in Psalms 86:12, showing a practical connection between obedience and worship.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 86:7 give to those who call upon the Lord in trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord will answer them
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:7 promises that when the psalmist calls upon the Lord in the day of trouble, God will answer, which encourages believers to trust and pray during difficulties, a theme supported by verses 1-6.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:8, what makes God unique compared to other gods?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:8 affirms that among the gods there is none like the Lord and no works like His, underscoring His unmatched uniqueness and power.

questions.question: Psalms 86:9 teaches that only the people of Israel will worship the Lord.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:9 states that all nations made by God shall come and worship before Him, indicating a universal worship rather than exclusive to Israel.

questions.question: What does Psalms 86:11 imply will happen if the psalmist’s heart is united to fear God's name?
options: He will walk in God's truth
He will be free from all troubles
questions.correctAnswer: He will walk in God's truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:11 links the uniting of the psalmist’s heart to the fear of God’s name with walking in God’s truth, implying that reverence for God leads to living a life of integrity and obedience.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:10 support the psalmist's prayer in the surrounding verses?
options: By affirming God's greatness and wondrous deeds, encouraging trust
questions.correctAnswer: By affirming God's greatness and wondrous deeds, encouraging trust
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:10 emphasizes God's greatness and wondrous works, reinforcing the psalmist's prayer for guidance and trust found in verses 7-9 and 11-12.

questions.question: What does Psalms 86:12 reveal about the psalmist's response to God's mercy?
options: He will praise and glorify God with all his heart forever
He will seek revenge on enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He will praise and glorify God with all his heart forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:12 shows the psalmist's heartfelt praise and glorification of God as a response to God's mercy, which is also highlighted in verses 5 and 13.

questions.question: If a believer follows the instruction of Psalms 86:11 to walk in God’s truth, what does Psalms 86:12 suggest will naturally follow?
options: Wholehearted praise and glorification of God
questions.correctAnswer: Wholehearted praise and glorification of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:11 asks for teaching to walk in God's truth, and Psalms 86:12 follows with the psalmist’s commitment to praise and glorify God with all his heart, showing that obedience leads to worship.

questions.question: Psalms 86:10 teaches that God is one among many gods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:10 clearly states that God is God alone and does wondrous things, denying the idea of multiple gods.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 86 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 86.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:13, from where has God delivered the soul of the psalmist?
questions.correctAnswer: The lowest hell
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:13 states, 'For great is thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell,' showing the psalmist's deliverance from the depths of despair or Sheol.

questions.question: In Psalms 86:14, who are described as rising against the psalmist?
options: The proud and assemblies of violent men
The nations and kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The proud and assemblies of violent men
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states, 'O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought after my soul,' indicating the opposition faced by the psalmist.

questions.question: Which attributes of God are highlighted in Psalms 86:15?
options: Compassion, graciousness, longsuffering, mercy, and truth
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion, graciousness, longsuffering, mercy, and truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:15 describes God as 'a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth,' emphasizing these divine qualities.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request from God in Psalms 86:16?
options: To turn unto him, have mercy, give strength, and save him
To judge his enemies and bring justice
To grant him riches and honor
questions.correctAnswer: To turn unto him, have mercy, give strength, and save him
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says, 'O turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; give thy strength unto thy servant, and save the son of thine handmaid,' showing a plea for divine aid.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:17, what is the purpose of God showing the psalmist a token for good?
options: So that those who hate him may see it and be ashamed
So that the nations may fear the Lord
So that the psalmist may gain wealth
So that the enemies may be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: So that those who hate him may see it and be ashamed
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states, 'Shew me a token for good; that they which hate me may see it, and be ashamed,' indicating the vindication of the psalmist.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's mercy and deliverance as found in Psalms 86:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 2:4-5
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:4-5 speaks of God's great mercy and love, making us alive with Christ, which echoes God's mercy and deliverance expressed in Psalms 86:13.

questions.question: The plea for God to 'turn unto me and have mercy' in Psalms 86:16 reflects a recurring theme in which Old Testament prophetic book?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah
questions.explanation: Isaiah frequently includes pleas for God’s mercy and turning to His people (e.g., Isaiah 55:7), paralleling Psalms 86:16's request for mercy and strength.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified in Psalms 86:15 where contrasting human pride is opposed to God's compassion and mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Verse 15 contrasts 'the proud' (verse 14) with God’s 'compassion, graciousness, longsuffering, mercy and truth,' an example of antithesis highlighting opposing qualities.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 86:14 states that the proud set God before them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:14 says the proud and assemblies of violent men 'have not set thee before them,' meaning they do not acknowledge God.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist promises to praise God with all his heart in Psalms 86:12.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:12 states, 'I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart,' confirming the psalmist's commitment to wholehearted praise.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'longsuffering' in Psalms 86:15 most closely means:
questions.correctAnswer: Slow to anger
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'erekh appayim' translated 'longsuffering' means 'slow to anger,' reflecting God’s patience as described in Psalms 86:15.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:13’s deliverance from the 'lowest hell' foreshadow New Testament teachings on salvation?
options: It prefigures deliverance from death and hell through Christ’s resurrection
It predicts eternal punishment without hope
It emphasizes earthly wealth as salvation
It focuses on military victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures deliverance from death and hell through Christ’s resurrection
questions.explanation: The psalmist's deliverance from the 'lowest hell' (Sheol) in Psalms 86:13 foreshadows the salvation through Christ’s resurrection discussed in 1 Corinthians 15:55-57.

questions.question: Which theme in Psalms 86:17 is also highlighted in 2 Corinthians 12:9 regarding God's help?
options: God’s help brings shame to enemies and comfort to the believer
God’s help leads to material prosperity
God’s help is reserved only for the righteous elite
God’s help is conditional on perfect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s help brings shame to enemies and comfort to the believer
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:17 and 2 Corinthians 12:9 both emphasize that God’s help brings comfort to the believer and causes adversaries to be ashamed.

questions.question: Which other Psalm shares a similar theme of God’s mercy and refuge as found in Psalms 86:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 103
questions.explanation: Psalm 103 extensively praises God’s mercy, compassion, and grace, paralleling the attributes described in Psalms 86:15.

questions.question: What is the significance of the psalmist identifying himself as 'the son of thine handmaid' in Psalms 86:16?
options: It reflects humility and a servant relationship with God
It indicates a status of priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects humility and a servant relationship with God
questions.explanation: The phrase shows humility and reliance on God, emphasizing a servant-master relationship, as seen in Psalms 86:16.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 86 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 86 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily emphasized in Psalms 86:5, highlighting God's readiness to forgive and abundant mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:5 explicitly states that the Lord is 'plenteous in mercy' and 'ready to forgive,' emphasizing God's attribute of mercy.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:13, what has God delivered the psalmist's soul from?
questions.correctAnswer: The lowest hell
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states God delivered the soul from 'the lowest hell,' indicating divine salvation from the depths of death or Sheol.

questions.question: What request does the psalmist make in Psalms 86:11 regarding his spiritual walk?
options: To teach him God's way and unite his heart
To grant him riches and honor
questions.correctAnswer: To teach him God's way and unite his heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:11 says, 'Teach me thy way... unite my heart to fear thy name,' indicating a desire for guidance and wholehearted devotion.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:8 characterize the Lord in relation to other gods?
options: He is similar to other gods
He is above all gods with unmatched works
He is a god among many
He shares authority with other gods
questions.correctAnswer: He is above all gods with unmatched works
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states 'Among the gods there is none like unto thee,' emphasizing God's uniqueness and incomparable works.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Psalms 86:2 and Psalms 86:16 reveal about the believer's relationship to God?
options: The believer is holy and requires no mercy
God saves and strengthens His servant who trusts in Him
The believer is self-sufficient without God
questions.correctAnswer: God saves and strengthens His servant who trusts in Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 86:2 calls God to save His servant who trusts Him, and 86:16 asks for strength and salvation for the servant, showing God's saving and strengthening role.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is primarily taught by Psalms 86:15 describing God as 'full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth'?
options: The doctrine of God's mercy and grace
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's mercy and grace
questions.explanation: Verse 15 highlights God's compassion, grace, longsuffering, mercy, and truth, teaching the doctrine of divine mercy and grace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:9 speak to the universal scope of God's worship in the redemptive narrative?
options: All nations made by God will worship Him and glorify His name
God is worshiped only in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: All nations made by God will worship Him and glorify His name
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states 'All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee,' pointing to the universal redemption and worship of God.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed by the psalmist’s confidence in Psalms 86:7 that God will answer in the day of trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The psalmist’s certainty that God will answer prayers in trouble (verse 7) reveals God’s faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 86:14, what characterizes the adversaries who rise against the psalmist?
options: They are proud and violent, setting not God before them
questions.correctAnswer: They are proud and violent, setting not God before them
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes the adversaries as proud and violent men who do not set God before them, indicating rebellion and opposition.

questions.question: What synthesis of Psalms 86:4 and Psalms 86:12 reveals about the psalmist’s attitude toward God in times of distress?
options: The psalmist is indifferent to God’s presence
The psalmist lifts up his soul to God and praises Him with all his heart
The psalmist seeks only material blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist lifts up his soul to God and praises Him with all his heart
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows the psalmist lifting up his soul to God, and verse 12 commits to praising God with all heart, demonstrating devotion amid distress.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that prayer is ineffective and unanswered. What does Psalms 86:3-6 actually teach about prayer?
options: Prayer is rarely heard by God
Prayer is a daily cry that God mercifully attends to and answers
Prayer is only symbolic and has no real effect
Prayer should be avoided in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is a daily cry that God mercifully attends to and answers
questions.explanation: Verses 3-6 show the psalmist crying daily to God, who is merciful and attentive to prayers, affirming prayer’s efficacy.

questions.question: What theological insight about sanctification is revealed by the psalmist’s plea in Psalms 86:2, 'for I am holy'?
options: Believers are made holy as servants of God, requiring His preservation
God does not acknowledge human holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are made holy as servants of God, requiring His preservation
questions.explanation: Verse 2 reveals the psalmist's identity as holy and God's servant, implying that holiness is connected to divine preservation and relationship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 86:10 affirm the monotheistic confession of God’s nature within the biblical narrative?
options: By acknowledging many gods of equal power
By declaring God as great, doing wondrous things, and being God alone
By equating God with created beings
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring God as great, doing wondrous things, and being God alone
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explicitly states God’s greatness, wonders, and exclusivity as 'God alone,' affirming biblical monotheism.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 86:1 and Psalms 86:17 provide about human dependency and divine deliverance?
options: Humans are self-sufficient and need no help
The psalmist is poor and needy, asking God to show a sign of help and comfort
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist is poor and needy, asking God to show a sign of help and comfort
questions.explanation: Verse 1 expresses human poverty and neediness; verse 17 petitions God for a token of good, revealing dependency on divine mercy and comfort.

questions.question: What does Psalms 86:13 teach about the nature of God's mercy in relation to human salvation?
options: God’s mercy is limited and temporary
God’s mercy is great and delivers from the lowest hell
God’s mercy is conditional on human works
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy is great and delivers from the lowest hell
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states 'great is thy mercy' and God has delivered the psalmist from the lowest hell, showing mercy as powerful and saving.
